record.paper_title: Quantum Communication: From Fundamentals to Recent Trends, Challenges and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can practical quantum communication systems generate single photons deterministically, rather than relying on stochastic spontaneous parametric down-conversion, when single-photon states are used as the quantum states of light and photon polarization can represent qubit states such as |0⟩, |1⟩, and an equal superposition?

evidence.quote: The most common way of realizing quantum communication is by means of photons, since they satisfy the fundamental requirements of quantum states, such as, having the ability of being entangled and in superposed state. Note that single photon states act as the quantum states of light. The challenge here is to develop mechanisms that can generate single photons.

This process of Spontaneous Parametric Down Conversion (SPDC) can generate one in 10଺ single photons using the existing technology [50] [51]. However, to be noted that this method, although is able to produce single photons, the generation is still stochastic. For practical implementations, we need a mechanism that can generate single photons deterministically.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a quantum communication setting in which qubits are encoded in the polarization degree of freedom of single photons, with logical states |0⟩ and |1⟩ identified with two orthogonal polarization modes and equal superpositions (|0⟩+|1⟩)/√2 obtainable by appropriate polarization rotations. A "single-photon source" is a physical device that, upon a trigger, emits an optical pulse containing exactly one photon in a prescribed spatiotemporal and polarization mode. Spontaneous Parametric Down-Conversion (SPDC), in which a nonlinear crystal pumped by a laser produces signal/idler photon pairs with a probability per pump pulse on the order of 10⁻⁶, is a stochastic source: the emission times of single photons are random and the probability of zero or multi-photon events is non-negligible.

Devise a physically realizable mechanism that, on demand (deterministically), emits a single photon in a chosen polarization mode with high purity (vanishing multi-photon component), high indistinguishability between successively emitted photons, and high collection/extraction efficiency, so that the source can serve as a practical building block for polarization-qubit quantum communication systems.
artifact.status_search_result: Deterministic single-photon sources based on semiconductor quantum dots have made substantial experimental progress, with recent demonstrations of high-purity, high-indistinguishability emission (e.g., >90% two-photon interference visibility in the telecom C-band) and successful use in field-installed QKD links. Reviews in 2025 indicate the technology is approaching commercial readiness, although simultaneously optimizing purity, indistinguishability, efficiency, and wavelength for scalable networks remains an active engineering challenge.

status_evidence.title: The hunt for the perfect single-photon source
status_evidence.snippet: A deterministic single-photon source is one where you push a button and it emits one and only one photon.
status_evidence.claim: Deterministic on-demand single-photon sources are an active and partially achieved goal.

status_evidence.title: Deterministic quantum dot single-photon sources: operational principles and state-of-the-art specifications
status_evidence.snippet: Quantum dot-based deterministic single-photon sources have reached a level of maturity where they are ready for commercialisation.
status_evidence.claim: Quantum-dot platforms provide deterministic single-photon emission with maturing performance.

status_evidence.title: Deterministic and highly indistinguishable single photons in the telecom C-band
status_evidence.snippet: Raw two-photon interference visibility of up to (91.7 ± 0.2)% in the telecom C-band.
status_evidence.claim: Telecom-band deterministic sources have been demonstrated with high indistinguishability.

status_evidence.title: QKD using deterministic single-photon sources over a field-installed fibre link
status_evidence.snippet: Quantum key distribution using deterministic single-photon sources over field-installed fibre.
status_evidence.claim: Deterministic sources have been deployed in practical QKD experiments.
